mlxPinsSource: https://pypi.org/pypi/mlx-vlm/0.6.17/json requires_dist (mlx>=0.32.0, transformers>=5.14.0); mlx and transformers pinned to the newest stable release satisfying those bounds with macOS arm64 wheels

appSupportDir.note: All runtime, model, venv and log files live under the app support directory. Nothing is installed system-wide and sudo is never used.

layout.mlxVenv: mlx-venv (python virtual environment for the MLX route)

llamaCpp.note: The tarball extracts to llama-b10752/ containing llama-server and its dylibs. The binary must run from inside that directory (dylibs are resolved relative to it).

model.name: UI-Mate-9B

memoryRecommendation.note: Measured on an M3 Max with 36 GB (2026-09-03): Q6_K weights (7.7 GB) + f16 mmproj (0.9 GB) + a 32768-token context hold about 11.5 GB of GPU memory during inference (llama-server RSS about 10 GB). 24 GB machines work but leave little room for a browser; 16 GB machines need a smaller quant (IQ4_XS or Q4_K_M from the same repo), a 16384 context, or an external endpoint. 8192 tokens is too small: one full-screen Retina capture is about 7,600 image tokens and the second step of a subtask overflows it.

model.contextSizeNote: 32768 tokens. The official Mac command uses -c 8192, which overflows on the second full-screen Retina screenshot of a subtask (measured 10,571 tokens); the KV cache for 32768 costs about 1.4 GB more GPU memory than 8192 on this runtime.
model.imagesToKeepNote: 8 screenshots kept in history (the official agent default is 5). Measured on llama.cpp b10752: dropping the oldest non-initial screenshot rewrites the prompt and invalidates the server's prefix cache, so every later step re-encodes all kept screenshots (imagesToKeep 2 made window steps cost 20 s instead of 10 s from the third step on). Keeping 8 means a subtask of up to 8 steps never collapses; with the desktop app's 1920 px long-edge cap, 8 screenshots plus history stay under 24k tokens of the 32768 context. Sessions reset per subtask.
model.maxTokensNote: Reply cap for the managed runtime. The official agent default is 16384; UI-Mate normally answers in 100-330 tokens, but one observed reply ran to about 1,300 tokens of thinking and took 70 s at 32 tok/s. 2048 bounds a step to about 65 s of generation; a truncated reply fails the step as invalid_action instead of hanging the run.

sampling.note: The official UI-Mate evaluation defaults are temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / enable_thinking true. Apprentice lowers the temperature to 0.2 (near-greedy decoding for a policy that must hit a specific control) and turns thinking off: measured 2026-09-04 on 32 real-window grounding cases, thinking off scored 17/32 and thinking on 16/32 at temperature 0.2, with 71 vs 150 median completion tokens. Re-check with pnpm bench:grounding when the model changes.

model.parallelSlotsNote: llama-server slots (-np). One client (the app) means one slot; with the default 4 slots a request can land on a cold slot and re-prefill the whole prompt (observed 8,900-token re-prefill, 40 s, while a benchmark shared the server).

mlx.diskNote: Estimates only (not measured on this machine): the bf16 upstream checkpoint (~19 GB) lands in the Hugging Face cache, the converted 6-bit weights are roughly 7-8 GB.
mlx.patchPolicy: No upstream cache patch is applied by default. Opt in with --patch <diff> --patch-sha256 <hash>; the hash is verified before git apply --check, and every touched file is recorded in mlx-venv/PATCHES.json.
